title: Inside the Multilingual Transformer: Computational Neuroanatomy of Shared and Language-Specific Brain Alignment
finding: Against multilingual fMRI, the shared cross-language alignment of multilingual encoders tracks attention-side computation more than the feed-forward layers usually credited with meaning.
summary: I looked inside multilingual encoders and compared their internal signals against multilingual fMRI data. The interesting part: the shared cross-language alignment seems to come more from attention-side computations than the usual 'semantic FFN' story.
whyItMatters: A single benchmark score does not tell you what part of the model is doing the work. This gives multilingual model builders a more inspectable target.

title: Language-Neutral or Language-Specific? Disentangling Multilingual LLM Subspaces with Naturalistic fMRI
finding: Separates shared multilingual structure from language-specific residue in XLM-R and NLLB-200, with naturalistic fMRI as the reference.
summary: This paper separates shared multilingual structure from language-specific leftovers in XLM-R and NLLB-200 using naturalistic fMRI data. Less 'does it work?', more 'what kind of representation is it using?'.
whyItMatters: Useful when you want to audit whether a multilingual encoder is carrying meaning across languages or just getting good at language-specific residue.

title: SOAR: Recovering Operational Overlays from Shared Semantics in Frozen Language Models
finding: Adds operational behaviours such as strict JSON or exact quotation to a frozen model as small overlays that can be tested on their own.
summary: A method for adding operational behaviors like strict JSON or exact quotation on top of a frozen model without retraining the whole thing. The goal is to make output contracts reusable and testable.
whyItMatters: Teams keep needing small, boring behavior guarantees from large models. This treats those guarantees as something you can isolate, ship, and audit.

title: Selective Revocation and Replay: Post-Compromise Recovery of Explicit Persisted State in Memory-Augmented LLM Agents
finding: Recovers a compromised agent's memory by tracing where poisoned state came from, revoking what descended from it and replaying only what needs repair.
summary: A recovery method for poisoned agent memory. Instead of wiping everything, it tracks where bad state came from, revokes descendants, and replays only the parts that need repair.
whyItMatters: Agent memory is useful until it carries attacker garbage forward. This gives operators a cleaner option than 'delete everything and hope'.

title: Same-Size Capability Transfer Reveals a Performance-Localization Tradeoff in Deterministic Function Calling
finding: A locked testbed for moving function-calling ability between same-size models, which measures the trade-off between raw performance and how localized the transferred capability is.
summary: A locked testbed for moving function-calling behaviour between same-family models. It compares sparse transfer against a dense module on a deterministic metric.
whyItMatters: It gives model-editing claims a deterministic check instead of a few cherry-picked examples.

title: Surgical Post-Training Diffing: Partial Recovery Without Clean Small-Mask Separation
finding: Paired diffing of Gemma post-training that localizes part of the capability signal in sparse weight changes and tests it on held-out evaluation.
summary: A paired diffing study of Gemma post-training. It recovers part of the capability signal from sparse differences and checks it against held-out evaluation.
whyItMatters: It separates 'we found the circuit' from 'we found something that generalizes', with a held-out test for each.

title: ProbeRoute: Probes as Routing Priors for Frozen-Backbone Multi-Token Prediction
finding: A cheap offline probe pass initialises routing for multi-token prediction on a frozen backbone, for better speculative drafting with the same recipe.
summary: A cheap probe pass is used to initialize routing for multi-token prediction on a frozen backbone. The aim is better speculative drafting without making the adaptation recipe bigger and messier.
whyItMatters: If you can get a better route from a small offline probe, you should not need to unfreeze half the model just to test the idea.

title: When Accuracy Hides Path Dependence: Criterion Fidelity in LLM Judges
finding: LLM judges can score accurately while reacting to how a criterion is worded instead of what it asks. Paraphrase and counterfactual checks expose it.
summary: This paper tests whether LLM judges follow the actual criterion or just react to how the criterion is worded. Accuracy can look fine while the judge is still path-dependent in a way you would not want in production.
whyItMatters: Good judge pipelines need to survive paraphrase and counterfactual checks. Otherwise the reviewer is grading the wording, not the work.

title: Binary Evidence Sufficiency Dissociation in Reasoning-Model Hidden States
finding: Reasoning models carry an internal signal for having enough evidence, separable from getting the final answer right.
summary: A probe study asking whether reasoning models carry an internal signal for 'I have enough evidence now.' That signal appears separable from just getting the final answer right.
whyItMatters: For retrieval and agent systems, knowing when the model has enough evidence may matter more than another confident-looking answer.

title: Structured Yet Fragile: Signed Intervention Geometry of Matched ORF and CRISPR Cell Painting Profiles
finding: A locked analysis of matched ORF and CRISPR Cell Painting profiles that maps the signed geometry of genetic interventions and tests how far it holds under stricter checks.
summary: A locked analysis of matched ORF and CRISPR Cell Painting profiles. It measures the signed geometry of the interventions and how well it supports retrieval under strict checks.
whyItMatters: Locked analyses show which biological claims hold when analytic flexibility is taken away.

title: Outcome Is Not Verification: Auditing Hidden-State Verifiers with Counterfactual Local Validity
finding: Audits hidden-state verifiers by separating a correct final answer from a locally valid process, with counterfactual tests.
summary: An audit of hidden-state verifiers that separates 'the final answer was right' from 'the process was locally valid.' Those are easy to blur and dangerous to confuse.
whyItMatters: If a verifier is just reading outcome signals, it should not be sold as process verification. This paper gives teams a way to check that.

title: First-Unsafe-Step Counterfactual DPO for KPI-Gaming in Autonomous LLM Agents: Held-Out Evaluation Under a Capability-Safety Bottleneck
finding: Finds the first unsafe step in an agent's trajectory, rewrites it safely and trains on the contrast, then measures the effect on held-out KPI-gaming tasks.
summary: A held-out agent-safety study: find the first unsafe step, rewrite it safely, and train on that contrast with preference optimization.
whyItMatters: It shows where preference training for agent safety gets its leverage, and what the base model's own behaviour limits.

title: What Survives Control Calibration? A Full-Scope Negative Result for a Locked Minimum-Description Acceptance Criterion
finding: A locked, full-scope test of a minimum-description acceptance rule for causal abstractions, calibrated against controls before any claim is made.
summary: A locked causal-abstraction acceptance rule, applied across the full scope of tested settings and calibrated against controls.
whyItMatters: Interpretability needs clear acceptance rules fixed in advance. This one sets the bar and reports exactly what clears it.

title: CacheMedic++: Robust KV-Cache Stabilization via Self-Distillation
finding: Corrupts, diagnoses and repairs KV-cache failures reproducibly with self-distillation, so serving instability becomes something you can test.
summary: A reproducible way to corrupt, diagnose, and repair KV-cache failures using distillation. The goal is to turn weird serving instability into something you can actually test.
whyItMatters: Serving failures are easier to fix when they are repeatable. This makes that repeatability part of the workflow.

title: CertiPatch: Specification Repair for Frozen Language Models with Replayable Empirical Certificates
finding: Repairs a frozen model against its specification: find counterexamples, patch the behaviour, and leave certificates anyone can replay.
summary: A repair workflow for frozen models that finds counterexamples, patches the behavior, and leaves behind replayable certificates.
whyItMatters: Model repair should not be a vibes-based sign-off. This turns it into something teams can rerun and inspect.

title: ScrubID: Identifiability-Aware Auditing for Mechanistic Interpretability
finding: Checks whether a mechanistic interpretability claim is identifiable from the evidence before anyone accepts it.
summary: An audit method for checking whether interpretability claims are actually identifiable from the evidence. Pretty plots are not enough.
whyItMatters: It raises the bar for interpretability claims by asking what can be independently checked.

title: Discover-Then-Distill: Separating Test-Time Adaptation from Self-Distillation Consolidation
finding: A compute-matched pipeline that separates short-term test-time adaptation from durable improvement through self-distillation.
summary: A compute-matched pipeline that separates short-term adaptation from durable improvement. The boring question matters: did we improve the model, or just help it survive the test?
whyItMatters: It helps teams avoid mistaking temporary adaptation for a real tuning win.

title: Robust Discover→Distill Under Poisoned Distillation Data
finding: Stress-tests the distillation step of a self-improving loop with corrupted and trigger-poisoned demonstrations, and measures which cheap defences hold.
summary: I isolated the distillation step of a Discover→Distill loop and fed it corrupted and trigger-poisoned demonstrations on a controlled synthetic benchmark, then measured a format gate and an Anchor-KL penalty as defences.
whyItMatters: A self-improving model that learns from its own archive of demonstrations has an attack surface in that archive. This sets up a reproducible way to test defences for it.

title: AvalancheLLM: Token-Layer Activation Event Cascades in LLMs under Gain Scaling
finding: Maps token-layer activation cascades under gain scaling, to find instability inside the model before it shows up as behaviour.
summary: A controlled study of activation cascades under gain changes. It looks for instability patterns in the model before they show up as weird behavior downstream.
whyItMatters: If a model becomes brittle under small scaling changes, you want to find out in a lab, not from users.

title: RIA: Retokenization Invariance Atlas
finding: A deterministic audit of formatting changes that keep a prompt's meaning and still change the answer.
summary: A deterministic audit for cases where semantically identical prompt formatting still changes the answer. Newline roulette is not a reliability strategy.
whyItMatters: It gives teams evidence about whether formatting changes are harmless or quietly changing outcomes.

title: CIS Technical Report
finding: Deterministic checks, evidence gates and implementation notes for teams that have to ship AI systems.
summary: A practical reliability report for AI systems: deterministic checks, evidence gates, and implementation notes for teams that have to ship the thing, not just demo it.
whyItMatters: It turns the reliability philosophy into something a delivery team can actually adopt.
